question.problem:
Which of the following gives the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x={e}^{t}-t,\,y={e}^{t}+t
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [0,e]?$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}-t) \\  & ={e}^{t}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{e}({e}^{t}+t)({e}^{t}-1)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a positive number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\ge 0$ for all $t\in [0,e].$

Therefore, the area is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{e}({e}^{t}+t)({e}^{t}-1)\,\text{d}t.
$$
